As per the facts of present case, on 25.12.2015, at about 4.00 P.M, deceased Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey S/O Sheetal Deen was working as Safai Karamchari in Ambience Cathering Apartment at outer Road, near Mixer Plant, Gurugram, Haryana within the jurisdiction of P.S DLF,PhaseII,
Gurugram, Haryana.
When a Activa Scooty bearing No. DL9SBD0310 came from the side of Ambience Mall at a very high speed, being driven in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased received serious injuries.
He was removed to Neelkanth Hospital, Mehrauli Road, Gurugram, Haryana and thereafter to Max Hospital, Sushant Lok and finally shifted to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi where he died on 26.12.2015.

sentences.text: the body of deceased Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey was conducted in Safdarjung Hospital N Delhi.
The present case pertains to the death of Sh Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that the accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.1/ Driver) who was driving Scooty bearing No.DL 9SBD0310.
Sh Rahul Malik, the owner of offending vehicle is made as respondent no. 2/owner.
As the offending vehicle was insured with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited hence Insurance Company is made as respondent no. 3.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioners have filed the present claim application thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 40,00,000/ (Forty Lacs ) from respondents as compensation, alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
3. The respondent No.1 and 2 have not filed any reply/W.S to the petition.
4. The respondent no.3, insurance company has admitted the fact that offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.3 at the relevant time, in the name of respondent No.2.
It is stated that the accident in question had taken place due to sole negligent of driver of other vehicle .
It is stated that R.1 was not having D/L to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

5. After completion of the pleadings, following issues were framed on 15.12.2016 :
(i) Whether Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey S/O Sheetal Deen sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 25.12.2015 caused due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Scooty) No. DL9S BD0310 being driven by respondent No.1 owned by respondent No.2 sand insured by respondent No.3. ?

OPP. 
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
(iii) Relief.
6.
In order to prove their claim, petitioners have examined petitioner No.1 Chedana as PW1 and Sh Pradip Paswan as an eye witness as PW2.
The respondent No.3 has examined Sh Gautam Bhatnagar, Manager ( Legal) as R3W1 in support of its case.
7. I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.1.
None appeared on behalf of respondent No.2 to argue the case.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission made by them and I also perused the record.

My issuewise findings are as under:
ISSUE NO. 1: (i) Whether Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey S/O Sheetal Deen sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 25.12.2015 caused due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Scooty)
No. DL9S BD0310 being driven by respondent No.1 owned by respondent No.2 sand insured by respondent No.3. ? OPP.
Chhedana vs Ashu Kashyap on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193676383/
6 8.

To prove this fact petitioners examined PW2 Sh Pradip Paswan , as an eye witness, who has deposed that on 25.12.2015, at about 4.00 P.M, he alongwith deceased Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey were working in Ambience Cathering Apartment at outer Road, near Mixer Plant, Gurugram,
Haryana.

He has deposed that when they were cleaning the road, a Activa Scooty bearing No. DL 9SBD 0310 came from the side of Ambience Mall at a very high speed, being driven in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased received serious injuries.
He has deposed that he has removed Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey to Neelkanth Hospital, Mehrauli Road, Gurugram.
09. I have gone through the testimony of PW 2 ( who is eye witness) who has proved the fact of accident being occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of scooty bearing No. DL 9SBD0310 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey.
10.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Scooty bearing No. DL9SB D0310 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
11.
The Petitioner no.1 is the wife , petitioner 2 to 5 are sons,of the deceased, as such LRs of victim.
12. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
PW1 Chedana, who is wife of the deceased has deposed that her husband was 40 years of age at the time of accident.
She has deposed that at the time of accident, the deceased was working in Ambience Catherina Apartment and earning Rs.15,000/ p.m
But petitioners have not examined any witness to prove the income of the deceased or produced any substantial evidence to prover the income of deceased.

However Ld Counsel for the petitioners fairly admitted that he has not placed on record any document qua showing the income of petitioner and submits that income of the petitioner may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.
So this Tribunal while assessing the income of deceased under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Haryana has assessed the income of deceased under the head of unskilled labour as Rs.8,769.30/p.m.

And as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and further addition of income @ 40% in the monthly salary of victim.

sentences.text: 13. The deceased was having five LRs, hence deceased/victim is presumed to be spending 1/4th of his income on his personal expenses.

And, therefore, the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.9,207.77/
(8,769.30/ + 3,507.72/ - 3069.25) per month. .
14.
The age of the deceased was 40 years ( As per the post mortem report attached with the criminal charge sheet Ex PW1/6) at the time of accident.
To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 15 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 16,57,398.60/ (9,207.77/ x 12 x 15. ).
This amount of Rs.16,57,398.60/ is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

15. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioners no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.17,000/ for funeral expenses, Rs.17,000/ for loss of estate and Rs. 2,20,000/ (Rs. 44,000/ each to all the petitioners) for loss of consortium, making a total sum of compensation as Rs.19,11,398.60/

The Detail of the whole award amount is: i. Loss of dependency Rs. 16,57,398.60/ ii. Funeral expenses Rs. 17,000/ iii. Loss of Estate Rs. 17,000/ v. Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/ to each Rs.
2,20,000/ petitioner Total Rs. 19,11,398.60/
16.
Now question arises who will pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.
17. The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted respondent No.1 was not possessing any valid D/L at the time of accident.

In this regard R3 has examined R3W1 Gautam Bhatnagar, as R3W1 who has proved the copy of notice U/O 12 rule 8 CPC Ex R3W1/1 and original postal receipts vide which the notice was sent to R.1 and R.2, vide Ex R3W1/2 and Ex R3W1/3.
He has proved copy of insurance policy vide Ex R3W1/4.He has deposed
that the offending vehicle was being driven by R.1 in contravention of insurance policy as R.1 was having only Lerner's license.
18. I have also perused the charge sheet filed by the petitioner on record.

As per the charge sheet respondent No. 1 was driving the offending vehicle without having a driving licence hence he has been charge sheeted for the offence U/S 279/304A IPC and Section 3/181 of M.V Act.
So there is violation of insurance policy.

19. This issue is therefore decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner is entitled for compensation from respondent no.3, who in turn has a right to recover the same from respondent no.1 and 2 jointly and severally after making payment to the petitioner.
ISSUE NO.3 (RELIEF)
20. Petition in hands is allowed.

Respondent no.3 is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 19,11,398.60/ (
Round of to Rs. 19,11,500/) alongwith interest @ 7.5% p.a from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 28.01.2016 till the date of compliance i.e., 11.02.2024.

Amount of interim compensation (if any)
be deducted from this amount.
Thereafter interest @ 12% p.a for delayed payment.

The awarded amount shall remain as tax free in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case in R/Special Civil Application No.4800 of 2021 titled The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd Vs Chief Commissioner of Income Tax (TDS) decided on 05.04.2022 Chhedana vs Ashu Kashyap on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193676383/

5. After completion of the pleadings, following issues were framed on 15.12.2016 :
(i) Whether Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey S/O Sheetal Deen sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 25.12.2015 caused due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Scooty) No. DL9S BD0310 being driven by respondent No.1 owned by respondent No.2 sand insured by respondent No.3. ?
OPP. 
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Ram Ahore @ Ram Ashrey died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Scooty bearing No. DL9SB D0310 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.facts:
When a Activa Scooty bearing No. DL9SBD0310 came from the side of Ambience Mall at a very high speed, being driven in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased received serious injuries.
He was removed to Neelkanth Hospital, Mehrauli Road, Gurugram, Haryana and thereafter to Max Hospital, Sushant Lok and finally shifted to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi where he died on 26.12.2015.
As the offending vehicle was insured with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited hence Insurance Company is made as respondent no. 3.
Hence insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication.
But petitioners have not examined any witness to prove the income of the deceased or produced any substantial evidence to prover the income of deceased.
However Ld Counsel for the petitioners fairly admitted that he has not placed on record any document qua showing the income of petitioner and submits that income of the petitioner may be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act.
So this Tribunal while assessing the income of deceased under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Haryana has assessed the income of deceased under the head of unskilled labour as Rs.8,769.30/p.m.
And as per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and further addition of income @ 40% in the monthly salary of victim.
And, therefore, the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.9,207.77/
(8,769.30/ + 3,507.72/ - 3069.25) per month. .
14.
The age of the deceased was 40 years ( As per the post mortem report attached with the criminal charge sheet Ex PW1/6) at the time of accident.
To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 15 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 16,57,398.60/ (9,207.77/ x 12 x 15. ).
As per the charge sheet respondent No. 1 was driving the offending vehicle without having a driving licence hence he has been charge sheeted for the offence U/S 279/304A IPC and Section 3/181 of M.V Act.
So there is violation of insurance policy.
